LESSON: ACIDS AND BASES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Physical Chemistry
Topic 2.1: Acids and bases
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 30

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Acids and bases, part of Physical Chemistry in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How are acids and bases applicable in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Acids and bases together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: The learner develops teamwork by contributing to group decision making while

working with peers as they carry out laboratory experiments and activities.

● Digital literacy: The learner interacts with digital technology as they search for information on the applications of

acids and bases

● Self-efficacy: the learner confidently determines the pH of different solutions and presents the findings to peers in

class

Values:
Responsibility: The learner develops accountability as they take care of apparatus while using them during experiments.

30

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):Environmental issues (safety in the laboratory): The learner observes

safety when handling acids and bases.

Suggested learning resources

Tactile braille label, large print labels, digital devices with assistive technology, reagents, talking colour detectors, talking

ammeters or voltmeter, tactile pH scale strips, volume measuring apparatus with tactile stops.

Suggested Key Skill(s)

• Describe five chemical properties of acids and bases in aqueous solution.

• Illustrate four applications of acids and bases in day to day life.

31
